You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group number 13, conventionally P2/c with Hall symbol −P 2yc. The supplied input cell is monoclinic with lattice parameters a = 5.84547 Å, b = 4.749686 Å, c = 4.96663203 Å, α = 89.042144°, β = 90.0°, and γ = 90.0°, containing 12 atoms with the declared input composition Zn₂Mo₂O₈. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s. Here the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0), while the matrix P maps the input basis into the standard setting by sending the first standard coordinate to the input b coordinate, the second standard coordinate to the input a coordinate (the listed coefficient is 0.9999999999999999 with a negligible −4.974685477397636×10⁻¹⁷ coupling to b), and the third standard coordinate to the negative of the input c coordinate, with only numerically negligible off-diagonal terms of order 10⁻¹⁹. Thus the transformation is essentially an interchange of the a and b axes combined with reversal of the c axis, with no origin displacement, allowing the original input cell to be recovered from the standard description.

In the standard frame, the asymmetric unit contains four independent crystallographic orbits, all position values being rounded to six decimal places. Zinc occupies the twofold Wyckoff site 2f with coordinate relation (1/2, y, 1/4); its representative atom lies at (0.5, 0.690315, 0.25), so the only free parameter is y = 0.690315 and the second zinc atom is generated by the monoclinic symmetry of P2/c. Molybdenum occupies the twofold site 2e with relation (0, y, 1/4), represented by (0.0, 0.184803, 0.25), again with y = 0.184803 as the sole independent coordinate and the second molybdenum produced by symmetry. Both the Zn and Mo atoms therefore lie on the z = 1/4 layer, with zinc fixed at x = 1/2 and molybdenum at x = 0.

The eight oxygen atoms divide into two inequivalent fourfold general-position orbits, each of type 4g with coordinate relation (x, y, z). The first oxygen orbit has representative position (0.256738, 0.374089, 0.405557), giving the three independent parameters x = 0.256738, y = 0.374089, and z = 0.405557; the remaining three oxygens of this orbit are generated by the space-group symmetry. The second oxygen orbit is represented by (0.215773, 0.105127, 0.938264), with independent parameters x = 0.215773, y = 0.105127, and z = 0.938264, likewise expanding to four symmetry-related atoms. Together, the 2f zinc orbit, the 2e molybdenum orbit, and the two distinct 4g oxygen orbits account for the full 12-atom contents of the cell, and no positional corrections beyond the stated six-decimal rounding are required.
